The four primitives form a unified mathematical framework for managing data scarcity, user experience, contractual obligations, and model validation. The Data Coverage Score quantifies the raw material input, while the UX Clarity Metric measures how effectively we communicate its limitations to stakeholders. The Licensed Data Requirement acts as a binary enforcement mechanism, ensuring only合规 data flows into our models. Finally, the Backtesting Scaffold provides empirical proof that our algorithms perform well on historical data. Together, they create a closed-loop system where data quality drives product perception, which in turn guides data acquisition strategies. This structure mirrors information theory: we maximize useful information (coverage) while minimizing noise (conflicts) and ensuring secure transmission (licensing). The primitives also dualize naturally: high coverage enables better backtesting, which improves UX clarity, which justifies higher licensing fees. Failure occurs when any link breaks—missing data, poor communication, contract violations, or invalid models.
